library(nlmixr2lib)

# Models and source

Dorey 2017 measured the in vitro killing of two pig pneumonia pathogens,
*Pasteurella multocida* and *Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae*, by florfenicol,
in an artificial broth and in pig serum. For each organism and growth matrix it
fitted a sigmoid Emax model of the 24 h change in bacterial count against the
PK/PD index AUC24h/MIC, and it reports the four parameter sets side by side in
Tables 4 and 5. All four are packaged, one file per fit, sharing this vignette.

| Model file | Organism | Growth matrix | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Dorey_2017_florfenicol_Pmultocida_broth` | *P. multocida* | CAMHB broth | Table 4, Broth |
| `Dorey_2017_florfenicol_Pmultocida_serum` | *P. multocida* | pig serum | Table 4, Serum |
| `Dorey_2017_florfenicol_Apleuropneumoniae_broth` | *A. pleuropneumoniae* | Columbia broth + NAD | Table 5, Broth |
| `Dorey_2017_florfenicol_Apleuropneumoniae_serum` | *A. pleuropneumoniae* | pig serum | Table 5, Serum |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dorey_2017_florfenicol_Pmultocida_broth"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0177568> (PMCID: PMC5446118, open access)

```{r stems}
fits <- tibble::tribble(
  ~fit,                ~organism,              ~matrix,
  "Pmultocida_broth",        "P. multocida",        "broth",
  "Pmultocida_serum",        "P. multocida",        "serum",
  "Apleuropneumoniae_broth", "A. pleuropneumoniae", "broth",
  "Apleuropneumoniae_serum", "A. pleuropneumoniae", "serum"
) |>
  mutate(stem = paste0("Dorey_2017_florfenicol_", fit))
```

```{r descriptions, results = "asis"}
cat("**`", fits$stem[1], "`** -- ",
    rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(fits$stem[1]))$description, "\n\n", sep = "")
```

The paper has no structural PK model. Plasma florfenicol was analysed
non-compartmentally, so the PK/PD index enters the models as the covariate
`AUCMIC_FLOR` and there is no PKNCA section in this vignette: no drug
concentration is simulated.

# Population

The pharmacodynamic "population" is a panel of six EU field isolates of each
organism (UK, France and Germany), taken from cases of pig pneumonia. They were
chosen because they grew logarithmically in both broth and pig serum, were
florfenicol-susceptible by disk diffusion, and spanned the broth MIC range (the
highest, the lowest and four intermediate). Geometric mean MICs (SD) were 0.42
(0.13) ug/mL in broth and 0.30 (0.16) ug/mL in serum for *P. multocida*, and
0.38 (0.11) and 0.39 (0.17) ug/mL for *A. pleuropneumoniae* (Results, "Minimum
inhibitory and mutant prevention concentrations").

Time-kill curves used eight static florfenicol concentrations, 0.25 to 8 times
the isolate's MIC, over 24 h, each isolate in triplicate, with a maximum count
of 1 x 10^10 CFU/mL and a quantification limit of 33 CFU/mL (Methods, "PK/PD
modelling"). Because the concentration is constant, the index is AUC24h/MIC =
24 h x (MIC multiple), from 6 to 192 h. The sigmoid Emax model was fitted per
isolate in WinNonlin and the six estimates averaged; Tables 4 and 5 give the
mean and the SD across isolates.

The plasma PK used for PK/PD integration came from 34 healthy Landrace Cross
male pigs, about 2 months old and 32.5-52.0 kg, given 15 mg/kg florfenicol
intramuscularly as one of two bioequivalent products (17 pigs each). Table 1
reports geometric mean Cmax 3.04 mg/L, AUC 53.7 h*mg/L and Cl/F 0.23 L/h/kg.

# Source trace

| Item | Value(s) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Sigmoid Emax equation, E = E0 + Emax * Ce^N / (EC50^N + Ce^N) | -- | Figure 2 |
| Ce = AUC24h/MIC (h) | covariate `AUCMIC_FLOR` | Figure 2; Tables 4-5 |
| `e0` (row 'Log E0') | 2.50 / 2.43 / 2.80 / 2.46 | Table 4 Broth / Serum; Table 5 Broth / Serum |
| `emax` (row 'Log Emax') | -7.02 / -6.39 / -5.30 / -5.29 | same |
| Span `emax - e0` (row 'Log Emax - Log E0') | -9.52 / -8.83 / -8.10 / -7.75 | same |
| `lec50` (row 'AUC24h/MIC50 (h)') | log(35.7) / log(32.3) / log(31.1) / log(42.1) | same |
| `lhill` (row 'Gamma') | log(3.10) / log(3.63) / log(3.06) / log(3.62) | same; also Results text, "PK/PD breakpoints" |
| `addSd` | fixed(0) | not reported |
| Breakpoints at E = 0, -3, -4 (validation targets) | see below | Tables 4-5 |

# The equation and its sign convention

Figure 2 prints `E = E0 + Emax * Ce^N / (EC50^N + Ce^N) x 100`, and Tables 4
and 5 print three effect rows: 'Log E0' (control growth, positive), 'Log Emax'
(the 24 h change in the presence of florfenicol, negative) and 'Log Emax - Log
E0' (the difference). Two readings of the coefficient multiplying the sigmoid
are possible: the 'Log Emax' row itself, or the span 'Log Emax - Log E0'. They
are separated by the breakpoints, which the paper reports in rows of their own:
invert each reading of the curve at E = 0, -3 and -4 and compare.

```{r published}
pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~fit,                      ~e0,  ~emax_row, ~span_row, ~ec50, ~hill, ~bp_static, ~bp_cidal, ~bp_4log,
  "Pmultocida_broth",        2.50, -7.02,     -9.52,     35.7,  3.10,  25.7,       40.2,      47.0,
  "Pmultocida_serum",        2.43, -6.39,     -8.83,     32.3,  3.63,  24.2,       37.3,      43.9,
  "Apleuropneumoniae_broth", 2.80, -5.30,     -8.10,     31.1,  3.06,  24.6,       43.8,      58.6,
  "Apleuropneumoniae_serum", 2.46, -5.29,     -7.75,     42.1,  3.62,  30.1,       58.4,      79.6
)

# Index giving effect E on a sigmoid that starts at e0 and moves by `coef`.
# NA when E lies outside the curve's range.
invert_sigmoid <- function(E, e0, coef, ec50, hill) {
  fr <- (E - e0) / coef
  ifelse(fr > 0 & fr < 1, ec50 * (fr / (1 - fr))^(1 / hill), NA_real_)
}

readings <- pub |>
  tidyr::crossing(target = c(0, -3, -4)) |>
  mutate(
    published = case_when(target == 0 ~ bp_static, target == -3 ~ bp_cidal, TRUE ~ bp_4log),
    coef_span = invert_sigmoid(target, e0, span_row, ec50, hill),
    coef_emax_row = invert_sigmoid(target, e0, emax_row, ec50, hill)
  )

readings |>
  select(fit, target, published, coef_span, coef_emax_row) |>
  mutate(across(c(coef_span, coef_emax_row), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(
    "Model" = fit, "Effect E (log10)" = target, "Published AUC24h/MIC (h)" = published,
    "Coefficient = span" = coef_span, "Coefficient = 'Log Emax' row" = coef_emax_row
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r sign-gate}
# GATE 1: the span reading is closer to the published breakpoint for every one
# of the twelve targets. Where the 'Log Emax' reading is NA, the curve never
# reaches the target at all, which by itself rules that reading out.
stopifnot(all(is.na(readings$coef_emax_row) |
  abs(readings$coef_span - readings$published) <
    abs(readings$coef_emax_row - readings$published)))
stopifnot(sum(is.na(readings$coef_emax_row)) == 5)

# The table rows are internally consistent: 'Log Emax - Log E0' equals the
# difference of the two rows above it to the printed rounding.
stopifnot(all(abs((pub$emax_row - pub$e0) - pub$span_row) <= 0.011))
```

The coefficient is the span, so the canonical `emax` is the 'Log Emax' row and
each model computes `E = e0 + (emax - e0) * Ce^N / (Ce^N + EC50^N)`. The
trailing "x 100" in Figure 2 is a typesetting error: it would stretch the curve
across hundreds of log10 units, whereas Figure 3 runs from about +2 to -6.

# Simulating the four models

```{r solve-helper}
# Solve one packaged model at a vector of AUC24h/MIC values. The models have no
# ODE state; each observation row returns the sigmoid at that row's covariate.
solve_index <- function(stem, values) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_along(values), time = 24, evid = 0, amt = NA_real_,
                   AUCMIC_FLOR = values)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(stem), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == length(values), !anyNA(out$Cc))
  out$Cc
}

grid <- c(0, seq(1, 200, by = 1))
curves <- fits |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(fit = fit, organism = organism, matrix = matrix,
          aucmic = grid, effect = solve_index(stem, grid)) |>
  ungroup()
stopifnot(nrow(curves) == 4 * length(grid))
```

## Replicating Figure 3

Figure 3 is an example curve from one unidentified isolate and matrix, with
observed points at 0, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 96, 144 and 192 h (0.25 to 8 x MIC).
The figure below shows the four mean-parameter curves with the same three
reference lines: bacteriostasis (E = 0), bactericidal action (E = -3) and a 4
log10 reduction (E = -4).

```{r figure-3, fig.cap = "Mean-parameter sigmoid Emax curves for the four Dorey 2017 fits, in the format of Figure 3 of Dorey 2017 (change in log10 CFU/mL over 24 h against AUC24h/MIC)."}
ggplot(curves, aes(aucmic, effect, colour = organism, linetype = matrix)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, -3, -4), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "AUC24h/MIC (h)", y = "Change in log10 CFU/mL over 24 h",
       colour = "Organism", linetype = "Growth matrix") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-8, 4)) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Validation gate: the published breakpoints

The decisive check inverts the packaged models themselves, by root-finding on
`rxSolve()` output rather than on a copy of the equation, at the three effect
levels the paper reports.

```{r breakpoint-gate}
invert_model <- function(stem, target) {
  uniroot(function(x) solve_index(stem, x) - target, c(1e-6, 1e4), tol = 1e-8)$root
}

bp <- readings |>
  left_join(fits |> select(fit, stem), by = "fit") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(simulated = invert_model(stem, target)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published)

bp |>
  select(fit, target, published, simulated, pct_diff) |>
  mutate(simulated = round(simulated, 1), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename("Model" = fit, "Effect E (log10)" = target,
         "Published AUC24h/MIC (h)" = published,
         "Packaged model AUC24h/MIC (h)" = simulated, "% difference" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable()

# GATE 2a: the packaged files reproduce the closed-form inversion of the
# transcribed parameters (both sides use the same numbers, so this is tight).
stopifnot(max(abs(bp$simulated - bp$coef_span)) < 0.06)

# GATE 2b: P. multocida, whose inter-isolate SDs are small, reproduces all six
# published breakpoints within 5%.
stopifnot(all(abs(bp$pct_diff[grepl("^Pmultocida", bp$fit)]) < 5))

# GATE 2c: every breakpoint of every fit is within 20%, and every packaged
# bacteriostatic breakpoint is within 15%.
stopifnot(all(abs(bp$pct_diff) < 20))
stopifnot(all(abs(bp$pct_diff[bp$target == 0]) < 15))
```

The published breakpoints are means of six per-isolate breakpoints, while the
packaged curve uses the means of the six per-isolate parameters. The two agree
only when the isolates are alike, because the breakpoint is a nonlinear
function of the parameters. *P. multocida* isolates were alike (EC50 SD 2.8-3.1
h) and agree within 4%. Agreement is weakest for *A. pleuropneumoniae* in serum,
the fit the paper itself flags for large inter-isolate variability (EC50 SD
14.5 h, breakpoint SDs 13.7-23.6 h). There the packaged curve gives 34.1, 53.5
and 65.7 h against published means of 30.1, 58.4 and 79.6 h.

## Validation gate: structural behaviour

```{r structure-gate}
chk <- curves |>
  group_by(fit) |>
  summarise(at_zero = effect[aucmic == 0], lowest = min(effect),
            monotone = all(diff(effect) <= 1e-12), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(pub |> select(fit, e0, emax_row, ec50), by = "fit")

# GATE 3: each curve starts exactly at e0, falls monotonically with exposure,
# and never passes emax.
stopifnot(all(abs(chk$at_zero - chk$e0) < 1e-9))
stopifnot(all(chk$monotone), all(chk$lowest >= chk$emax_row - 1e-9))

# GATE 4: at the index equal to EC50 the effect is exactly halfway between e0
# and emax, which is what makes EC50 the AUC24h/MIC50 of Tables 4 and 5.
half <- mapply(function(stem, ec50) solve_index(stem, ec50), fits$stem, pub$ec50)
stopifnot(max(abs(half - (pub$e0 + pub$emax_row) / 2)) < 1e-9)
```

# Using the models with the plasma PK

Table 2 of Dorey 2017 integrates the plasma PK with the mean MICs. Its
Cav0-24/MIC column times 24 h is the AUC0-24/MIC of the first day after a 15
mg/kg dose, and its Cav24-48/MIC column times 24 h is that of the second day.
Feeding those mean ratios to the matching model predicts the 24 h change in
count that a static exposure of the same size would produce. This is an
illustration of the models, not a reproduction: Dorey 2017 did not publish
these predictions, and plasma exposure falls over each day rather than being
static.

```{r integration}
tab2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~fit,                      ~cav0_24_mic, ~cav24_48_mic,
  "Pmultocida_broth",        3.78,         1.69,
  "Pmultocida_serum",        5.29,         2.37,
  "Apleuropneumoniae_broth", 4.18,         1.87,
  "Apleuropneumoniae_serum", 4.07,         1.82
) |>
  left_join(fits |> select(fit, stem), by = "fit") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    day1_index = 24 * cav0_24_mic,
    day2_index = 24 * cav24_48_mic,
    day1_effect = solve_index(stem, day1_index),
    day2_effect = solve_index(stem, day2_index)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

tab2 |>
  select(fit, day1_index, day1_effect, day2_index, day2_effect) |>
  mutate(across(-fit, \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename("Model" = fit, "Day 1 AUC24h/MIC (h)" = day1_index,
         "Day 1 change (log10)" = day1_effect,
         "Day 2 AUC24h/MIC (h)" = day2_index,
         "Day 2 change (log10)" = day2_effect) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r integration-gate}
# GATE 5: on day 1 every fit is past its own 4 log10 breakpoint, and on day 2
# every fit is still past bacteriostasis (net kill).
stopifnot(all(tab2$day1_effect < -4), all(tab2$day2_effect < 0))
```

On day 1 the mean index (about 90-130 h) is past the 4 log10 breakpoint of
every fit. On day 2 (about 40-57 h) every fit still predicts net kill, but the
size of the kill varies between the fits, as the table shows.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Population-mean parameters, not a population model.** Each parameter set is
  the mean of six per-isolate fits. The SDs in Tables 4 and 5 describe spread
  across isolates; they are not estimated variance components, so the models
  have no `eta` terms. The paper also reports no residual error, so `addSd` is
  fixed at 0 and the models are for typical-value simulation.
* **Index carried as a ratio.** `AUCMIC_FLOR` carries AUC24h/MIC directly. Each
  isolate was exposed to multiples of its own MIC, and only the geometric mean
  MIC of the six is reported, so no single MIC can split the ratio into an
  absolute exposure and a `mic` parameter. To use a model with a plasma
  exposure, form the ratio with the MIC of the isolate of interest, measured in
  the matching growth matrix.
* **Algebraic output, no bacterial state.** The fitted quantity is the 24 h
  change in log10 CFU/mL relative to the starting inoculum, so `Cc` is that
  change. The time-kill inoculum is not stated in Dorey 2017 (the Methods refer
  to an earlier paper), so no absolute bacterial count is modelled.
* **No PK model.** Plasma florfenicol was analysed non-compartmentally (Table 1
  gives Cmax, AUC, AUMC, Tmax, Cl/F and T1/2 only), so there is no PK model to
  package and no PKNCA comparison.
* **Dose predictions not reproduced.** The deterministic and Monte Carlo dose
  predictions (Tables 6-8) combine the breakpoints with Cl/F, a literature MIC
  distribution (Figure 4), a serum:broth MIC correction and the serum free
  fraction. The free fraction is given only in the Discussion (35%), and the
  corrected MIC inputs are not printed, so these tables are not recalculated
  here. The Table 6 doses are proportional to the serum breakpoints (dose per
  hour of breakpoint 0.208 mg/kg for *P. multocida* and 0.685 mg/kg for *A.
  pleuropneumoniae*), so the serum fits were the ones used.

```{r dose-proportionality}
# Table 6 deterministic daily doses (mg/kg) divided by the serum breakpoints of
# Tables 4 and 5: a constant ratio within each organism shows that the serum
# breakpoints were the input.
tab6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~organism,  ~dose_static, ~dose_cidal, ~dose_4log, ~bp_static, ~bp_cidal, ~bp_4log,
  "P. multocida",        5.05,  7.77,  9.15,  24.2, 37.3, 43.9,
  "A. pleuropneumoniae", 20.6,  40.0,  54.5,  30.1, 58.4, 79.6
) |>
  mutate(r_static = dose_static / bp_static, r_cidal = dose_cidal / bp_cidal,
         r_4log = dose_4log / bp_4log)
ratios <- as.matrix(tab6[, c("r_static", "r_cidal", "r_4log")])
stopifnot(all(abs(ratios[1, ] - 0.208) < 0.001), all(abs(ratios[2, ] - 0.685) < 0.002))
```

## Errata

* **Figure 2, "x 100".** The printed equation ends in "x 100"; this is a
  typesetting error (see "The equation and its sign convention" above).
* **Abstract breakpoint labels.** The Abstract calls 25.7, 40.2 and 47.0 h (*P.
  multocida*) and 24.6, 43.8 and 58.6 h (*A. pleuropneumoniae*) "serum
  breakpoint values". In Tables 4 and 5 these are the **broth** columns; the
  serum values are 24.2, 37.3 and 43.9 h and 30.1, 58.4 and 79.6 h. The
  Discussion quotes the serum *P. multocida* values (24, 37 and 43 h)
  correctly. The packaged models follow the tables.
* No published correction to Dorey 2017 was found (EuropePMC search,
  2026-11-25).
